security_audit.summary: All 142 static matches were adjudicated as false positives. Most matches are Markdown code fences, links, placeholder credentials, or template prose; the Python helper only runs a fixed git log command and optionally writes a requested changelog file. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, concealed execution, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The changelog helper accepts a revision argument for git log.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the optional since tag against known local tags or reject values beginning with a dash before invoking git.

remediation.issue: The changelog helper writes to a caller-provided path.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the output path may overwrite an existing file and offer an overwrite confirmation or a force flag.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples trigger broad static detections.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder credentials clearly marked as examples and avoid presenting executable-looking secrets in templates.

content.value_statement: Incomplete documentation makes projects difficult to adopt and maintain. This skill provides structures, templates, and helper workflows for clear Markdown documentation.
actual_capabilities: Creates README outlines with installation, usage, API, and contribution sections.
Formats changelogs using semantic versioning and conventional commit categories.
Generates a Markdown table of contents from heading levels.
Provides templates for contribution guides and technical documentation.
Explains Markdown code blocks, badges, links, and reference sections.
limitations: The helper only reads local Git history and does not create releases.
Link validation checks local Markdown links and skips external URLs.
Generated documentation needs project-specific facts and final review.
The helper does not verify badge accuracy or API examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare a project README
use_cases.description: Build a clear README structure with installation steps, examples, and contributor guidance.

use_cases.title: Draft release notes
use_cases.description: Turn local Git history into a categorized changelog for an upcoming release.

use_cases.title: Standardize internal guides
use_cases.description: Apply consistent headings, tables of contents, and code formatting to technical guides.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Markdown README outline for my Python package. Include installation, quick start, configuration, API reference, contributing, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Improve existing documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this README for missing sections, unclear wording, and inconsistent Markdown. Return a prioritized improvement plan before rewriting it.

prompt_templates.title: Generate release notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release notes from these Git commit messages. Group changes by Added, Changed, Fixed, Security, and Breaking Changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a documentation set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a documentation plan for this service. Define the README, setup guide, API reference, operations guide, and contribution guide, with required sections for each.

output_examples.input: Create a README outline for a command-line data tool.
Create release notes from conventional commits.
Generate a table of contents for a long guide.
output_examples.output: A nested list of links for each included heading, ordered by heading level.

best_practices: Use real project details instead of leaving template placeholders in published documentation.
Keep installation steps tested and aligned with supported versions.
Review generated changelogs before release to confirm categories and sensitive details.
anti_patterns: Do not publish example API keys or URLs as if they are production configuration.
Do not rely on badges instead of explaining project status and support boundaries.
Do not generate release notes without reviewing the underlying commit messages.

faq.question: What documents can this skill help create?
faq.answer: It supports README files, changelogs, contribution guides, and technical documentation.

faq.question: Can it generate a table of contents?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper can create a table of contents from Markdown headings.

faq.question: Can it create a changelog from Git history?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper groups local Git commits into common changelog categories.

faq.question: Does link validation check websites?
faq.answer: No. It checks local Markdown links and skips external URLs.

faq.question: Does it publish documentation or releases?
faq.answer: No. It prepares documentation content and writes a changelog only when requested.

faq.question: Should I use generated text without review?
faq.answer: No. Verify commands, versions, links, security guidance, and project-specific claims before publishing.
